sentences.text: Counsel for Petitioner :- Mohd. Shaafi,Shujauddin

Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.
Hon'ble Vivek Kumar Birla,J.
Hon'ble Vinod Diwakar,J.
1.
Heard Mohd. Hasam holding brief of Shri Shujauddin, learned counsel for the petitioners and Shri Virendra Kumar Pal, learned A.G.A. for the State respondents.

2. The present writ petition has been preferred with the prayer to quash the impugned First Information Report dated 02.11.2023, registered as Case Crime No. 383 of 2023, under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506, 307, 376, 511, 354 IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Hapur Dehat,
District Hapur and for a direction to the respondents not to arrest the petitioner in pursuance of Aslam And 4 Others vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others on 14 December, 2023

entities.text: Aslam And 4 Others vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177340361/
1
impugned
First Information Report.

3. At the very outset, learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that he may be permitted to withdraw the writ petition in so far as petitioner no.1- Aslam, who is the husband of the victim is concerned.
4. Prayer aforesaid is allowed.
5. The writ petition is dismissed as withdrawn only in so far as petitioner no.1-Aslam is concerned.
6. So far as other petitioners are concerned, we proceed to hear the matter on merits.

7. Submission of the learned counsel for the petitioners is that the marriage had taken place about 10 years back on 11.12.2013, therefore, allegation regarding demand of dowry are baseless and only on the basis of general allegations entire family members have been roped in the present case.

It is further submitted on bare reading of the impugned FIR the allegations under Sections 307 and 376 IPC are not made out against the petitioners, therefore, impugned FIR is liable to be quashed in so far as the petitioners no.2 to 5.
8. Matter requires consideration.

9. Learned AGA has accepted notice on behalf of respondent no.1 and 2.
10.
Issue notice to the respondent no.
3. Steps be taken within a week.
11. All the respondents may file counter affidavit within four weeks.
The petitioners shall have three weeks thereafter to file rejoinder affidavit.

12. List thereafter before the appropriate Bench.
13.

Till the next date of listing or till submission of police report under Section 173(2) Cr.P.C.,
whichever is earlier, the respondents are restrained from arresting the petitioners no.2 to 5 pursuant to the aforesaid FIR subject to cooperation in ongoing investigation.

Order Date :- 14.12.2023 Nitendra  Aslam And 4 Others vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others on 14 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177340361/
